h1: Rest Point Sampran Nakhon Pathom — Clean, Quiet, Free Parking for Drivers Passing Through
intro: If you're driving the Phetkasem highway through Nakhon Pathom and want somewhere quiet, clean and affordable for a single night — or a pit stop before heading into Bangkok — Rest Point Sampran is a small hotel many reviewers call good value. It sits right on Phetkasem Road in Khun Kaeo, Nakhon Chai Si, with around 17–18 rooms. Every room has air conditioning, TV, a fridge, free drinking water, and there's free parking out front. Rates start from approx. ฿600/night — in exchange for a simple roadside setup with no resort facilities, and cash-only payment.

body.html: Rest Point Sampran is a small, owner-run hotel on Phetkasem Road in Nakhon Chai Si district, on the side heading towards Bangkok. Its appeal is straightforward: clean, quiet rooms at a friendly price. It isn't a resort with a pool or big garden — it's a roadside hotel built for drivers who want a bed for the night, or a base to rest before continuing into Bangkok the next morning.

There are around three room types, from a single-bed room to a twin and a family room. Each room comes with air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, free drinking water and an en-suite bathroom with a shower, and some rooms have a small balcony to step out and catch the breeze. Rooms are sized for a comfortable night's sleep rather than spacious lounging, but they're well laid out and kept tidy.

The thing real guests praise most consistently is cleanliness and quiet. Reviewers describe very clean, quiet rooms that are easy to relax in, with a shower that runs at a good temperature, cold air conditioning and a fridge that actually works. Several mention the free bottled water set out for them, plus tea, coffee and a few snacks. For a roadside place in this price band, that level of care keeps most reviews positive.

"Very clean room, quiet, the shower temperature was just right, good A/C, and they left free bottled water and snacks. Easy parking right by the room — great value for a one-night stop before Bangkok."

Drivers also like the free parking right out front — you can pull up close to your room and unload easily — and there's a small cafe on site. Restaurants and convenience stores line Phetkasem Road nearby, so grabbing food is no trouble. Location-wise it's about 7 km from the Nakhon Chai Si district office, roughly 3.7 km from Wat Samphran (the dragon-wrapped tower temple), and around 6 km from Suan Sampran — handy if you're exploring the Nakhon Chai Si–Sampran side and want a bed nearby.

Set your expectations for a simple roadside stay. There's no breakfast, no pool, gym or lift (the building is around three storeys), and importantly it's cash only — bring enough cash. As an owner-run place, staff aren't on a full 24-hour desk like a chain hotel, so if you'll arrive late, let them know in advance. A few reviewers ran into awkward key hand-back coordination on an early checkout, so it's worth agreeing the details with the owner at check-in.

Overall Rest Point Sampran scores around 8.2 out of 10 from real guest reviews on the booking platforms. It isn't for anyone after a resort feel or a long list of facilities — but if your brief is a clean, quiet room with easy parking, in the few-hundred-baht range, right on Phetkasem Road for a single night or a stop along the way, it does that job well for the price. Rates start around ฿600 and nudge up a little by season and room type.

faqTitle: FAQ — Rest Point Sampran Nakhon Pathom

faq.q: Where is Rest Point Sampran in Nakhon Pathom, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Rest Point Sampran is at 9/51-53 Phetkasem Road, Khun Kaeo, Nakhon Chai Si District, Nakhon Pathom, right on the main Phetkasem highway heading towards Bangkok. It's about 3.7 km from Wat Samphran (the Dragon Temple), 2.5 km from the Thai Human Imagery Museum, and around 6 km from Suan Sampran. The Phra Pathom Chedi in Nakhon Pathom town is about 20 km away.

faq.q: How much does Rest Point Sampran cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿600/night. There are around three room types — single, twin and family rooms. Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge and free drinking water. Prices rise a little by season and room type, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Rest Point Sampran take credit cards?
faq.a: No — the hotel is cash only. Bring enough cash for the room and any deposit before you arrive, as you may not be able to pay by card on arrival.

faq.q: Does Rest Point Sampran have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: No breakfast, but there's free parking out front and a small on-site cafe. Every room has free bottled water plus tea, coffee and a few snacks. Phetkasem Road nearby has plenty of restaurants and convenience stores for an easy bite.

faq.q: Who is Rest Point Sampran best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for drivers passing through on Phetkasem who want a clean, quiet room with easy parking in the few-hundred-baht range — for a single night or a stop before Bangkok. It's not the pick for anyone after a resort feel, a pool or a riverside stay.

faq.q: Is Rest Point Sampran quiet, and are the rooms clean?
faq.a: Yes on both. Cleanliness and quiet are exactly what real reviewers praise most. Guests describe very clean, quiet rooms with a good-temperature shower and cold A/C. It's a simple roadside place, but the care shown keeps most reviews positive.
